name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,273

clue.text: Toy with sailor giving evidence in court?

blocks.note: a jack, or jack tar, is an old slang word for a sailor
a witness gives evidence standing in the witness box

explanation.surface: A sailor in the witness box, playing with a toy while testifying.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the court phrase is read loosely: a witness is 'in the box'. Put the sailor's nickname in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a children's plaything: a lidded case from which a puppet on a spring pops up.

clue.text: Pier initially just extended to take yachts

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: the leading letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A harbour pier has just been lengthened so that yachts can moor there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like it belongs to the pier's history, but it tells you to read the first letters of the five words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a structure built out from the shore into water where boats can tie up.

clue.text: Position on board costs Wren badly

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's place on a company board is costing a person called Wren dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a boardroom; it means aboard a ship. Wren also suggests the architect or a bird, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast, a station occupied by a sailor aboard.

clue.text: Artistic style sir’s mini poems deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight's short poems are put to use in some artistic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of the three middle words are used, and the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionism is a nineteenth-century painting movement led by Monet, Renoir and others, capturing light and fleeting moments.

clue.text: Sudden pain finally hit me around side

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so keep the closing letter of each of the next words
to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: final letter of hit
final letter of me
a wing is a side of a building, a team or a stage

explanation.surface: A sharp pain has struck someone at last, right in their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' covers both 'hit' and 'me', giving the two letters that wrap around the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a brief, sharp stab of discomfort, coming on suddenly and fading quickly.

clue.text: Remarkable routine supporting minor actor

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it is written after the other

blocks.note: an extra is a film actor with a tiny non-speaking part
routine as an adjective means ordinary, everyday

explanation.surface: A small-part actor gives a remarkable performance in a supporting role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' sounds like theatre jargon for a role, but in a down answer it places the routine word below the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary is beyond the usual, unusual enough to be worth comment, which is what remarkable means.

clue.text: Possess topless dress

indicators.note: without a top means the head is removed, so drop the opening letter

blocks.note: a gown is a long formal dress

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to have a dress with no upper part.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the G from the front of the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a thing is to have it as your property, the plain sense of possess as a verb.

clue.text: Crown Henry VIII

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Roman numeral eight

explanation.surface: The crown of King Henry VIII, England's much-married Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII seems to be one king; split him into an abbreviation and a number word.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its highest point or peak, as in the height of fashion or summer.

clue.text: Cavalry unit having bad time in retreat

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: poor means of low quality, bad
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cavalry squadron is having a rough time as it falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: The military 'retreat' fits the surface but also tells you to reverse the combined pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cavalry regiment a troop is the subdivision of a squadron, a small body of mounted soldiers.

clue.text: Forceful tennis playing by middle of set

indicators.note: playing suggests moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged
the middle of a word is its central letter, so keep only that

blocks.note: taken as written
central letter of set

explanation.surface: Powerful tennis being played midway through a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' fits tennis neatly, but it only supplies its central letter, added to the game's letters before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means having great strength or force, used of feelings, effort or play.

clue.text: Sure Japanese currency must finally reverse direction

indicators.note: the last letter is a compass point that turns to face the opposite way, so one letter is swapped

blocks.note: the yen is the money of Japan

explanation.surface: A confident instruction that the yen must now turn around and head the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: N for north is the final letter; reversing that direction gives S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure, used as an exclamation of agreement, is an informal way of saying yes.

clue.text: Artwork has English talking wildly

blocks.note: Eng is the abbreviation for English
raving is speaking incoherently or madly

explanation.surface: A painting or sculpture that seems to feature an Englishman ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly' looks like a rearrangement signal, but here it is part of the phrase meaning ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print or design cut into a metal plate or wood block, a type of art.

clue.text: One million news channels, note, direct

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for million
the media are the outlets that carry news
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A million viewers tune in to news stations, which are told to be straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' reads as a verb ordering someone about; it is the adjective meaning with nothing in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate can mean acting without any intervening agent, as in the immediate cause, which matches direct.

clue.text: Consecrate bishop in opposition to More

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
less is the opposite of more

explanation.surface: A bishop consecrating something in defiance of Thomas More, the Tudor statesman and saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes More look like Thomas More; it is just the comparative word, and its opposite is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to make holy or set apart for sacred use, which is what consecrating means.

clue.text: How contestant shows inability to answer in roundabout way?

definitions.text: How contestant shows inability to answer
definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, 'by pass', not a noun

blocks.clueFragment: How contestant shows inability to answer
blocks.note: first meaning: a quiz contestant who is stumped indicates it by saying 'pass'
second meaning: a road taking traffic around a town

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant dodging a question they cannot answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words for the quiz half: a contestant signals defeat by a pass. 'Roundabout' suggests a traffic circle, but it means indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a route avoiding a town centre, an indirect road around rather than through.

clue.text: Right give out task for committee

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
to emit is to give out light, heat or sound

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand out the proper job for a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective meaning correct, but it supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of activity officially assigned to a body, its terms of reference.

clue.text: Fruits galore? Half of those would show penny-pinching

indicators.note: keeping half of each word means the back halves are cut away

blocks.note: the front three of six letters
the front three of six letters

explanation.surface: Fruit in abundance, though only half of it, would suggest someone stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those' points back to the two opening words; take the front half of each.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal describes someone sparing and economical with money, and penny-pinching is a disapproving word for that.

clue.text: Mix up prior to cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, and in crosswords it signals letters being mixed into new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: stir everything together before you start cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Mix' alone is the definition and 'up' is fodder; 'cooking' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a medley of assorted things, such as dried petals or musical pieces, so a mixture.

clue.text: Medic with round in Washington

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: O is round in shape
Washington DC, the District of Columbia

explanation.surface: A doctor doing their rounds in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' suggests a doctor's ward rounds but gives the ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is an informal shortening of doctor, and a medic is likewise a colloquial word for a doctor.

clue.text: Trainee acted strangely

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee behaved oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The five letters of the verb are simply reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police, a learner in uniform.

clue.text: Stage scenery is becoming harder

blocks.note: first meaning: the backdrop and set of a play
second meaning: solidifying, as concrete or jelly does

explanation.surface: Theatre scenery that is gradually stiffening, like paint or plaster drying.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are joined by 'is'; the second is the participle used of glue, cement or jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's setting is its scenery and location, while setting also describes a liquid firming up into a solid.

clue.text: Preserve egg on the turn

indicators.note: something on the turn is turning round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Save an egg that is about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' sounds like food going sour, but it signals turning round the louse's egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To tin food is to can it, sealing it in a metal container so it keeps for a long time.

clue.text: Where people may recover honour?

definitions.note: read as two words, 'a ward', a place

blocks.note: first meaning: a room in a hospital where patients get better
second meaning: a prize or distinction conferred on someone

explanation.surface: A question about where people might get back their lost good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recover honour' reads as regaining reputation; split instead into a hospital place and a prize, with the answer read as two words for the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize or decoration given in recognition, just as an honour is bestowed for merit.

clue.text: Idleness of plummy Eton men disturbed without millions

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Posh-voiced old Etonians, upset at losing their fortunes, are left idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one M from the three words, then rearrange the twelve letters left. Eton is the English private school; plummy describes an upper-class accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemployment is the state of having no job, an enforced idleness from work.
